I've read that Dwayne Johnson wants to remake Big Trouble In Little China with him as Jack Burton. I'm very, very, VERY against a remake. It's one of Carpenter's best films, don't mess with perfection.

That being said, I'm all for a SEQUEL, but only if it's done right. I'd love to see Kurt Russel return as an older Jack Burton (his role in Guardians Of The Galaxy Vol. 2 proves he's still got it!), but in a new setting. How about "Big Trouble In Little Mexico" for something different than the first film? They could draw inspiration from ancient Aztec lore and mythology, something new for our sarcastic trucker hero Jack Burton to get caught up in. Danny Trejo could be his sidekick in this film. Cheech Marin could play a Mexican cab driver who's actually a hip wizard/supernatural expert (sorta like Egg Chen in the first movie). Jack Burton now drives a truck transporting frozen burritos to Mexico.

I got an idea. Jack Burton battles a human reincarnation of an evil ancient disposed Aztec goddess who wants to reclaim the Earth. She's powerful but uses Valley Girl colloquialisms and constant pop culture references, a Valley Girl god. That would be weird, a villain who's both humorous and dangerous. Something different than Lo Pan, yet just as off-the-wall. She wants to perform a ritual to open a portal and bring Quetzalcoatl to Earth. Only Jack Burton, Cheech Marin, and Danny Trejo can stop her and her cohorts.

I think it'd be a hit, at least with fans of the original film. Robert Rodriguez would be my choice to direct, with John Carpenter producing and composing the electronic music score.

Well guys, what do you think?
Make a Big Trouble In Little China SEQUEL instead of a pointless remake!
